Add the addresses or names of agents you know, such as a vendor's billing bot, so they are recognized.

boot.panel.noToken: This device has no boot token.

boot.revertedBy.other: Its watchdog ended the trial and it is on its default entry.

datactl.crashLoadError: Could not load the crash reports.
datactl.crashNone: No crash reports. The Hub has not crashed, or the reports were deleted.

datactl.deleteIntro: Delete everything on this Hub and start again from an empty Hub. Export first if you may need any of it.
datactl.deleteKept: Your owner account and this browser’s session stay, so you remain signed in. A new audit log starts with this deletion. Then the Hub restarts.
datactl.deleteWhat: Every account, chat, run, agent, memory, project, setting, file, device pairing, stored key and password, and the audit log on this Hub is deleted.
datactl.errors.notFound: It is no longer there. Reload the page and try again.
datactl.errors.validation: The Hub did not accept these values. Check them and try again.

datactl.exportStarted: Your download has started. The file is written as it downloads; keep this page open until it finishes.
datactl.importConfirmBody: Everything in the file is written to this Hub, all or nothing, and each table is checked against the file. Then the Hub restarts. You stay signed in, as the owner from the export.
datactl.importConfirmTitle: Replace this Hub with the export?
datactl.importDevices: The file has no passphrase, so this Hub keeps its own keys: paired devices must be added again, and Relay set up again if you use it.
datactl.importDone: The import is done and verified.
datactl.importEncrypted: This export is encrypted. Enter its passphrase to check it.
datactl.importFailed: The import failed. Nothing was changed.
datactl.importIntro: Move a Hub here: import an export into this Hub. It must be empty: a new Hub, or one after Delete all.
datactl.importNotEmpty: This Hub already holds data, so it cannot take an import. Delete all data first, or import into a new Hub.
datactl.importRestoredOff: What a file cannot vouch for comes back off: MCP servers that run as programs here, plugins and external agent programs are turned off, hooks need trusting again, and every other signed-in session is signed out.
datactl.intro: Everything on this Hub is yours. Export it, move it to another Hub, delete it, choose how long it is kept, and decide whether crash reports leave this machine.
datactl.migrates: Made by an older Nova: its data is brought up to date as it is imported.
datactl.overviewLoadError: Could not load this Hub's data overview.
datactl.ownerOnly: Only the owner of this Hub can manage its data.
datactl.passphraseHint: With a passphrase the file is encrypted and includes the stored keys and passwords. At least {min} characters; keep it safe, it cannot be recovered.
datactl.privacy: Nova never uses your data to train models, and it sends nothing about how you use it anywhere unless you turn something on here or in telemetry export.
datactl.reasons.archive_damaged: The file is not a complete Nova export. It may be damaged or cut short.
datactl.reasons.archive_inconsistent: The file refers to data it does not hold. It may be damaged, or it was not made by Nova.
datactl.reasons.busy: Another export, import or deletion is running. Try again when it finishes.
datactl.reasons.checksum_mismatch: Part of the export does not match its checksum: the file is damaged.
datactl.reasons.content_type: The file could not be sent. Try again.
datactl.reasons.crash_reports_off: Crash reports are off. Turn on sending first.
datactl.reasons.disk_full: There is not enough free disk space on the Hub to import this file. Free some space and try again.
datactl.reasons.foreign_secret: The file points to stored keys or passwords that it does not carry or that belong to a Hub itself, so it was refused. Nothing was imported.
datactl.reasons.hub_not_empty: This Hub already holds data. Delete all data first, then import.
datactl.reasons.hub_only: An export with a passphrase carries every stored key and password, so it can only be started from a browser signed in to the Hub, not from a paired device.
datactl.reasons.managed: Your organization's policy does not allow this.
datactl.reasons.newer_schema: This export comes from a newer version of Nova. Update this Hub first.
datactl.reasons.no_endpoint: No endpoint is set. Enter where crash reports go first.
datactl.reasons.passphrase_required: This export is encrypted. Enter its passphrase.
datactl.reasons.send_failed: The endpoint did not take the report.
datactl.reasons.ticket_expired: The download link expired. Start the export again.
datactl.reasons.too_large: The file is too large to import.
datactl.reasons.unsafe_path: The file names a folder or file outside where Nova keeps its data, so it was refused. Nothing was imported.
datactl.reasons.unsupported_format: This export is in a format this version of Nova cannot read.
datactl.reasons.verify_failed: What was written did not match the file, so nothing was imported. Try again; if it happens again, the file may be damaged.
datactl.reasons.wrong_passphrase: The passphrase is wrong, or the file was changed after it was exported.

firmware.change.afterRestart: Takes effect after the device restarts.
firmware.change.appliedRestarting: Applied. {device} is restarting with the watchdog armed.
firmware.change.applyBody: {n, plural, one {# setting changes on {device}.} other {# settings change on {device}.}} The values before are kept in a snapshot, so you can roll back.
firmware.change.approveRollback: Approve restoring the firmware settings of {device}
firmware.change.approved: Approved. Nothing has changed yet: apply it when you are ready.
firmware.change.asked: Approval requested. Answer it below or on the Approvals page.
firmware.change.lastDenied: Your last approval request was denied.
firmware.change.nextRestart: The settings take effect at its next restart, without the watchdog.
firmware.change.noRestart: These settings take effect without a restart.
firmware.change.noWatchdog: {device} has a BIOS admin password, which novad never keeps, so its watchdog could not restore the settings: Nova does not restart it.
firmware.change.restartHint: If {device} does not come back within {duration}, it restores the previous settings and restarts once.
firmware.change.restartYourself: Restart it yourself for the settings to take effect, and roll back from here if it misbehaves.
firmware.change.rollbackBody: {n, plural, one {# setting on {device} goes back to its value in the snapshot.} other {# settings on {device} go back to their values in the snapshot.}} A rollback does not restart the device: restart it yourself for the settings to take effect.
firmware.change.rollbackTitle: Roll back the firmware settings of {device}?
firmware.change.unsafe: These settings may not be safe: the watchdog could not restore everything, so {device} may still hold some of the new values. Check what it holds now, and roll the change back from here.
firmware.change.weakensOff: This change weakens security, and “Allow changes that weaken security” is off. {link}.
firmware.errors.alreadyDefault: This trial is already the default.
firmware.errors.applyFailed: Writing a setting failed. The device restored the previous settings.
firmware.errors.applyFailedUnrestored: Writing a setting failed and the device could not restore the previous settings. Check its firmware settings before it restarts.
firmware.errors.approvalDenied: The approval for this change was denied. Ask again, or plan a different change.
firmware.errors.approvalExpired: The approval for this change expired. Ask for approval again.
firmware.errors.approvalMismatch: This is not the change that was approved. Ask for approval again.
firmware.errors.approvalMissing: This change has no approval, so it was not sent.
firmware.errors.approvalRequired: This change needs your approval first.
firmware.errors.approvalWaiting: Your approval for this change is still waiting. Answer it first.
firmware.errors.attemptPending: A boot trial is already running on this device. Wait for it to finish, or revert it.
firmware.errors.authorizationExpired: The Hub’s signed authorization expired before the device got it. Check the clocks, then try again.
firmware.errors.authorizationRefused: The device refused the Hub’s signed authorization. Nothing was changed.
firmware.errors.badAnswer: The device sent an answer the Hub cannot read.
firmware.errors.baseMismatch: The settings on the device changed since the plan. Nothing was written: plan again.
firmware.errors.biosPassword: This machine needs its BIOS admin password. Store it in the BIOS admin password section first.
firmware.errors.busy: Another firmware operation is running on this device. Try again in a moment.
firmware.errors.consentRequired: Turning this on needs your explicit confirmation.
firmware.errors.failed: This change failed. Plan it again.
firmware.errors.firmwareDisabled: BIOS and firmware changes are off. Turn them on in Settings → Devices first.
firmware.errors.grubDefaultNotSaved: GRUB keeps a chosen default only with {setting}. Set it in {file} on the device, update GRUB, then make the entry the default again.
firmware.errors.hubOnlyAnswer: This approval can be answered only in Nova, by you.
firmware.errors.identity: The Hub’s identity key is not loaded, so it cannot sign the change. Check Network → Trust.
firmware.errors.interrupted: The Hub restarted while sending this change, so it is not known whether the device took it. Check the device, then ask again.
firmware.errors.kernelArgs: Kernel arguments are not supported yet: a profile boots an entry as its bootloader defines it.
firmware.errors.lowLevelBootOff: Low-level boot changes are off. Turn them on in Settings → Devices first.
firmware.errors.moduleNotAllowed: The firmware module is not allowed by this device’s policy.
firmware.errors.nameTaken: This device already has a boot profile with that name.
firmware.errors.noClientCertificate: The Hub has no client certificate for the device’s secure management channel yet. Check Network → Trust.
firmware.errors.notConfirmed: Only a trial the device confirmed can become the default.
firmware.errors.notMade: The device did not make the change.
firmware.errors.nothingToRollBack: Nothing to roll back: the device already has the settings of that snapshot.
firmware.errors.ownerOnly: Only the owner of this Hub can manage device firmware and boot.
firmware.errors.planMismatch: The device no longer has this plan. Plan the change again.
firmware.errors.rebootNotOffered: A rollback does not restart the device. Restart it yourself for the settings to take effect.
firmware.errors.rebootUnavailable: The device cannot restart itself: power actions are off in its novad settings.
firmware.errors.replayed: The device already used this authorization. Nothing was changed again.
firmware.errors.requestPending: A boot change for this device is already waiting for approval.
firmware.errors.rollbackFailed: The rollback failed on the device. Check its firmware settings before it restarts.
firmware.errors.rolledBack: This change was already rolled back.
firmware.errors.securityDegrading: This change weakens security, and changes like that are off. Turn on “Allow changes that weaken security” in Settings → Devices first.
firmware.errors.securityDegradingKeys: This change weakens security ({keys}), and changes like that are off. Turn on “Allow changes that weaken security” in Settings → Devices first.
firmware.errors.snapshotCorrupt: The Hub’s copy of the snapshot failed its check, so it was not used.
firmware.errors.snapshotMismatch: The device’s snapshot did not match its checksum. Nothing was changed.
firmware.errors.snapshotMissing: There is no snapshot to restore for this change.
firmware.errors.snapshotNotApplicable: That snapshot does not fit this machine’s settings now.
firmware.errors.snapshotUnreadable: The Hub’s copy of the snapshot cannot be read.
firmware.errors.tlsRequired: This needs the device’s secure management channel (mutual TLS), and the device has no certificate for it yet. Switch the Hub to its local CA in Network → Trust, then add the device again so it gets one.
firmware.errors.unexpectedDiff: The device planned a change you did not ask for, so Nova stopped. Nothing was changed.
firmware.errors.unknownEntry: The device has no boot entry with that id. Refresh and choose one it lists.
firmware.errors.unsupportedHardware: Nova cannot change this on this machine. {reason}
firmware.errors.unverifiedTrial: The device could not tell which entry it booted, so this trial is not verified. Check that it booted this entry, then confirm it.
firmware.errors.watchdogPending: A restart with the watchdog is already pending on this device. Wait for it to finish.
firmware.errors.watchdogUnavailable: The watchdog cannot restore a machine with a BIOS admin password, so Nova does not restart it. Apply without the restart, restart it yourself, and roll back from Nova if needed.
firmware.errors.watchdogUsed: The watchdog already handled this change.
firmware.hubOnly.notSentRetry: Your answer was not sent: try again.
firmware.hubOnlyLine: Only you can answer this, in Nova: here or on the Approvals page. Chat channels, email links and agents cannot answer it.
firmware.panel.allReadOnly: Every setting on this machine is read-only.
firmware.panel.anyOrder: Any order of the same entries

firmware.panel.canChangeAs: Nova can change the allowlisted settings below ({support}).
firmware.panel.chooseOne: Choose at least one new value.
firmware.panel.hasPassword: {device} has a BIOS admin password: Nova needs it to apply changes.
firmware.panel.historyFailed: Could not load the firmware history.
firmware.panel.matrixCaption: Which machines Nova can change firmware settings on (Linux only)
firmware.panel.matrixFailed: Could not load the support matrix.
firmware.panel.nowHint: Now {value}. Leave empty to keep it.
firmware.panel.offTitle: BIOS and firmware changes are off.
firmware.panel.offWhat: Turned on, you can change the settings below on supported machines. Each change is a dry run first, shows exactly what will change, keeps a snapshot, needs your approval here in Nova, and can be rolled back. Nova never changes firmware by itself. Reading the settings works either way.
firmware.panel.offWhy: They are off by default: a wrong firmware setting can keep a machine from starting, or weaken its security.
firmware.panel.orderHint: Move entries up or down; the first is tried first.
firmware.panel.passwordKept: It is kept in the Hub’s vault, sent to the device only with an approved change, and never shown again, here or anywhere.
firmware.panel.planIntro: Planning is a dry run: novad works out the diff and keeps a snapshot of the current values. Nothing changes on {device} until you approve and apply the plan.
firmware.panel.planned: Planned. Check the diff, then ask for approval.
firmware.panel.readFailed: Could not read the firmware settings.
firmware.panel.removeBody: Nova forgets it. The machine itself is not changed.
firmware.panel.removeBodyHas: Nova forgets it. Changes to this machine are refused until you store it again. The password on the machine itself stays as it is.
firmware.panel.removeTitle: Remove the BIOS admin password of {device}?
firmware.panel.revoked: This device was revoked: its firmware cannot be read.
firmware.panel.rollbackBody: Nova plans restoring the settings from before this change and asks for your approval on that diff. Nothing changes on {device} until you approve and apply it.
firmware.panel.rollbackBodyAt: Nova plans restoring the settings from before this change (its snapshot of {when}) and asks for your approval on that diff. Nothing changes on {device} until you approve and apply it.
firmware.panel.rollbackPlanned: Rollback planned. Approve it, then apply it.
firmware.panel.rollbackTitle: Roll back this firmware change on {device}?
firmware.panel.settingsCaption: The settings Nova may change (an allowlist); it never touches others

firmware.settings.consent.allowChanges.t: Allow BIOS and firmware changes on devices?
firmware.settings.consent.allowChanges.w: You can then change Wake-on-LAN, what happens after a power cut, boot order, virtualization, Secure Boot, the TPM and the fan profile on supported devices running novad.

It is off by default because a wrong firmware setting can keep a machine from starting. Every change is still a dry run first, shows exactly what changes, keeps a snapshot, needs your approval here in Nova, and can be rolled back. Nova never changes firmware by itself, and every change is in the audit log.
Allow low-level boot changes on devices?
You can then boot a device once into another bootloader entry, with a watchdog that sends it back to its default entry if it does not come back, and make a confirmed entry the default.
It is off by default because a machine booted into a broken entry can stay unreachable until someone is in front of it. Each change needs your approval here in Nova.
firmware.settings.consent.allowSecurityD: Allow firmware changes that weaken security?
This lets a firmware change turn Secure Boot or the TPM off. Without it, such changes are refused even when you approve them.
Leave it off unless a machine needs one of these off. Each such change still needs its own approval, and its diff marks what weakens security.
firmware.settings.consent.pxe.title: Serve network boot from this Hub?
firmware.settings.consent.pxe.what: The Hub then serves an iPXE menu and the files in its boot-images folder to any machine that presents a device’s boot token, without signing in. Each fetch is rate-limited and recorded in the audit log.
firmware.settings.consent.pxe.why: It is off by default because those images are readable by anyone holding a token. Nova runs no DHCP or TFTP server: you point your own DHCP server at the iPXE address.
firmware.settings.firmwareWatchdogHint: For firmware changes applied with a restart: how long the device has to come back before its watchdog restores the previous settings.
firmware.settings.intro: Changes below the operating system of devices running novad. All are off by default, apply to the whole Hub and are recorded in the audit log. Nova never makes these changes by itself.
firmware.settings.readFailed: Could not read the firmware switches.
firmware.settings.states.allowChangesOff: Off: devices refuse firmware changes. Reading their settings still works.
firmware.settings.states.allowChangesOn: On: you can plan firmware changes on supported devices; each needs your approval and can be rolled back.
firmware.settings.states.allowLowLevelOf: Off: devices refuse boot trials and new defaults. Clearing a pending one-shot always works.
firmware.settings.states.allowLowLevelOn: On: you can try a boot profile once on a device and make a confirmed one the default, each after your approval.
firmware.settings.states.allowSecurityDe: Off: changes that turn Secure Boot or the TPM off are refused, even when approved.
On: a firmware change may turn Secure Boot or the TPM off, after your approval.
firmware.settings.states.pxeOff: Off: the network boot addresses answer “not found”.
firmware.settings.states.pxeOn: On: the Hub serves the iPXE menu and its boot images to devices holding a boot token.

netsurface.fix.noListener: The Hub is still starting. If this lasts more than a minute, restart the Hub.

oob.endpoint.checkRedfish: Reads the BMC’s Redfish service. The first check reads its certificate, without credentials, for you to confirm.
oob.endpoint.confirm.after: Only after you confirm it does the Hub send the BMC its user name and password, and only to a BMC presenting this certificate.
oob.endpoint.confirm.question: Is this your BMC’s certificate?
oob.endpoint.confirm.read: The Hub read it without sending any credentials. Compare its fingerprint with the one on the BMC’s own web page or console, not one sent over this network:
oob.endpoint.confirmPin.description: Confirm only if this fingerprint is the one the BMC itself shows. From now on the Hub sends it the credentials, and refuses any other certificate at this address.
oob.endpoint.confirmPin.done: Certificate confirmed. The Hub may now send the BMC its credentials.

oob.endpoint.logEmpty: Nothing asked of this BMC yet.

oob.endpoint.mismatch.headline: This BMC presented a different certificate

oob.endpoint.runsAfter: It runs only after you approve it on the card that appears next, within 10 minutes.

oob.form.addDescription: A BMC is the management controller built into a server or a business computer. The Hub talks to it directly, never through the machine's operating system.
oob.form.addressHint: A host name or IP address.
oob.form.addressHintRedfish: A host name or IP address; https:// with a port also works.
oob.form.addressHintRepin: A new address is another BMC: its certificate is pinned again.
oob.form.deviceHint: The machine this BMC manages, so its page offers these actions.
oob.form.editDescription: Saving withdraws its approvals still waiting and its approved BIOS plans: an approval names the BMC as it was.
oob.form.errors.address: Enter the BMC’s host name or IP address.
oob.form.errors.name: Enter a name.
oob.form.errors.passwordLong: At most {n, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}.
oob.form.errors.pin: Enter the SHA-256 fingerprint: 64 hexadecimal digits, colons allowed.
oob.form.errors.systemId: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore only.
oob.form.errors.usernameBad: At most {n, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}, with no colon.
oob.form.name: Name
oob.form.passwordHint: Kept in the Hub's vault. Nova never shows it again.
oob.form.pinHint: Optional. From the BMC's own certificate page; entering it confirms it. Blank: the first check reads the certificate without credentials and you confirm its fingerprint, like an SSH host key. A different certificate later is refused.
oob.form.pinPlaceholder: Blank: confirm it after the first check
oob.form.repin.description: Read the fingerprint on the BMC's own certificate page (or its console), not from this network. Only that certificate will be accepted from now on.
oob.form.repin.label: New certificate fingerprint (SHA-256)
oob.form.repin.title: Pin a new certificate for {name}
oob.form.replace: Replace the user name and password
oob.form.replaceKeep: The stored ones are never shown. Leave this off to keep them.
oob.form.replaceNone: The Hub has none stored for this BMC: enter them again.
oob.form.systemIdHint: Only when the BMC manages several systems. Blank picks its only one.
oob.kindHelp.ipmi: Older BMCs, through ipmitool on the Hub. Power, sensors and next boot; no BIOS settings.
oob.kindHelp.redfish: Most current server BMCs (iDRAC, iLO, XClarity and others). Over HTTPS, with the BMC certificate pinned.
oob.page.about: Power, sensors, the next boot device and BIOS settings through a machine’s BMC (Redfish or IPMI), even when its operating system is down.
oob.page.emptyOff: Turn out-of-band management on, then add a machine’s BMC.
oob.page.emptyOn: Add the address and credentials of a machine’s BMC to manage it here.
oob.page.intro: Reach a computer through its BMC, the management controller built into servers and many business computers, over Redfish or IPMI: power it on or off, read its sensors, choose its next boot device or change BIOS settings, even when its operating system is down. Intel AMT is not available in this version.
oob.page.noClient: This version of the app cannot manage BMCs.
oob.page.noneLinked: No BMC is linked to this device.
oob.page.reachable: {device} can be reached through its BMC, below the operating system.
oob.page.stateOn: On, {n, plural, one {# BMC} other {# BMCs}}.
oob.page.unlinked: That BMC is not linked to this device any more.
oob.parts.amtNotBuilt: Intel AMT is not available in this version.
oob.parts.checkFirst: Check the connection first, then confirm the BMC’s certificate: the Hub sends it nothing else before that.
oob.parts.confirmPinFirst: Confirm the BMC’s certificate first (above): the Hub sends it nothing else before that.
oob.parts.consent.allows: Through them it can power a machine on, off, cycle or reset it, pick its next boot device and change its BIOS settings for the next restart, even when its operating system is down or unreachable.
oob.parts.consent.approvals: Every change waits for your approval in Nova and cannot be answered from a channel. Reading the power state, the sensors and the BIOS settings does not ask.
oob.parts.consent.audit: Everything is recorded in the audit log. Only the owner of this Hub can use it.
oob.parts.consent.connects: The Hub connects to the BMCs you add (the management controller built into a server or a business computer), with the user name and password you give it.
oob.parts.disable.description: Approvals still waiting are withdrawn. The BMCs and their credentials are kept, but nothing reaches them until you turn it on again.
oob.parts.disable.title: Turn off out-of-band management?
oob.parts.enable.description: Read what it allows before you turn it on.
oob.parts.enable.title: Turn on out-of-band management?
oob.parts.offHelp: Off by default: a BMC controls the hardware below the operating system, so a mistake can turn a machine off or keep it from starting. Nothing reaches a BMC while it is off.
oob.parts.onHelp: The Hub may reach the BMCs below. Every change still asks for your approval.
oob.parts.pin.notRead: Not read yet: the first check reads it
oob.powerEffect.cycle: The BMC turns the machine off and on again at once. The operating system does not shut down first, and unsaved work on the machine is lost.
oob.powerEffect.off: The BMC cuts the power at once (a hard power off). The operating system does not shut down first, and unsaved work on the machine is lost.
oob.powerEffect.on: The BMC turns the machine on.
oob.powerEffect.reset: The BMC restarts the machine at once (a hard reset). The operating system does not shut down first, and unsaved work on the machine is lost.
oob.reasons.apply_outcome_unknown: The BMC may have taken part of the change before it failed. Read the BIOS settings to see what is pending, then plan again.
oob.reasons.approval_expired: Nobody answered the approval in time.
oob.reasons.approval_mismatch: The approval did not cover this action, so it did not run.
oob.reasons.approval_not_by_user: Only your own answer in Nova runs an out-of-band action.
oob.reasons.bad_address: Enter a host name or an IP address in the usual dotted form. For Redfish, an https:// address with a port also works.
oob.reasons.bad_response: The BMC gave an answer Nova cannot use.
oob.reasons.base_mismatch: The BIOS settings changed since the plan. Make the plan again.
oob.reasons.bmc_auth_failed: The BMC refused the user name or password. Enter the credentials again.
oob.reasons.bmc_not_found: The BMC does not offer that.
oob.reasons.bmc_precondition_failed: The settings changed on the BMC in the meantime. Try again.
oob.reasons.bmc_session_failed: The BMC refused the IPMI session: it cannot be reached, or the credentials are wrong.
oob.reasons.bmc_timeout: The BMC did not answer in time.
oob.reasons.bmc_tls_failed: The secure connection to the BMC failed.
oob.reasons.bmc_too_large: The BMC’s answer was too large.
oob.reasons.bmc_unreachable: The BMC did not answer. Check its address and that the Hub can reach it.
oob.reasons.consent_required: Turning on out-of-band management needs your explicit consent.
oob.reasons.credentials_in_address: Put the user name and password in their own fields, never in the address.
oob.reasons.credentials_missing: The Hub has no credentials for this BMC. Enter them again.
oob.reasons.endpoint_changed: The BMC was edited, so its waiting approvals were withdrawn.
oob.reasons.firmware_changes_off: BIOS and firmware changes are off. Turn on “Allow BIOS/firmware changes” in Settings → Devices first.
oob.reasons.interrupted: The Hub restarted during the action; it was not run again.
oob.reasons.ipmitool_missing: ipmitool is not installed on the Hub, so IPMI BMCs cannot be reached. Install it on the Hub, or use Redfish.
oob.reasons.managed: Your organization’s policy sets out-of-band management; it cannot be changed here.
oob.reasons.no_pin: Check the connection first: that reads the BMC’s certificate.
oob.reasons.no_system: The BMC lists no system to manage.
oob.reasons.not_built: Intel AMT is not available in this version. Use the machine’s Redfish or IPMI BMC.
oob.reasons.not_redfish: That address does not answer as Redfish. Check it, or add the BMC as IPMI.
oob.reasons.not_supported_by_ipmi: IPMI cannot do that. BIOS settings and a one-time USB boot need the BMC’s Redfish address.
oob.reasons.nothing_to_change: Nothing to change: every chosen value is already set or not allowed.
oob.reasons.oob_disabled: Out-of-band management is off. Turn it on first.
oob.reasons.owner_only: Only the owner of this Hub can use out-of-band management.
oob.reasons.pin_changed: The BMC now presents another certificate than the one shown. Check the connection again and compare the new fingerprint.
oob.reasons.pin_unconfirmed: Confirm the BMC’s certificate first: the Hub sends it no credentials before that. Check the connection, then compare and confirm the fingerprint.
oob.reasons.plan_expired: The approval of this plan ran out. Make the plan again.
oob.reasons.plan_failed: Applying this plan failed earlier, so it cannot be used again. Read the BIOS settings and plan again.
oob.reasons.plan_target_changed: The BMC was edited since this plan was approved. Make the plan again.
oob.reasons.plan_used: This plan was already applied. Make a new plan to change more.
oob.reasons.redirect_refused: The BMC answered with a redirect, which Nova never follows. Enter the address the BMC serves itself.
oob.reasons.security_degrading: This change weakens security (Secure Boot or the TPM) and needs the separate override, which is off.
oob.reasons.system_not_found: The BMC has no system with that id. Check the system id.
oob.reasons.tls_pin_mismatch: The BMC presented a different certificate than the one pinned, so nothing was sent to it. If you replaced its certificate on purpose, re-pin it.
oob.reasons.unknown_device: That device is not on this Hub.
oob.reasons.unsupported_by_bmc: This BMC does not offer that action.
oob.reasons.unsupported_hardware: BIOS settings are not supported on this hardware through its BMC.
